title: Tech Note: Using the Power of the 4th Dimension Quick Report Editor
author: Walt Nelson

historical_commentary.text: This note demonstrates advanced formatting techniques within 4D's built-in Quick Report Editor (a WYSIWYG ad-hoc reporting tool distinct from the more code-driven Custom Reports), showing time calculations, blank note columns, alpha/numeric formatting tricks, sort/break levels, and boolean cross-tab logic via a worked Aircraft Maintenance Schedule example. The Quick Report Editor concept survives in spirit in modern 4D's reporting tools, but the specific 3.x-era editor UI and its exact formatting options have been superseded by newer report-generation tooling in later 4D versions.
related_updates: 4D's ad-hoc/quick reporting tools have been revised across many versions since 3.x, with modern equivalents offering different UI and capabilities than the 3.x-era Quick Report Editor described here
4D Write Pro and other modern presentation/reporting layers now offer additional ways to generate formatted output beyond the classic Quick Report Editor
